description: A ten-panel composite figure organised as five matched rows x two columns, combining Mössbauer transmission spectra (left column) with the corresponding hyperfine-field probability distributions P(B_hf) (right column). Row pairs are (a,b) α-Fe foil, (c,d) Fe-5Al, (e,f) Fe-6Al, (g,h) Fe-6.8Al and (i,j) Fe-9Al low-density steels. Left panels plot Transmission (%) versus Velocity (mm/s) (ticks -8 to 8, shared axis label under (i)); each shows the six-line sextet of bcc Fe, red data points with a black fitted envelope. The absorption lines broaden and become shallower with increasing Al: (a) spans 80-100% with minima near 80.5%, (c) 92-100%, (e) 90-100%, (g) 96-100%, (i) 96-100%. Right panels plot P(B_hf) against B_hf in T (18-36, ticks every 2 T). (b) shows a small hump near 20 T and a dominant sharp peak near 33 T reaching about 0.08. (d), (f), (h) and (j) show broad humps deconvoluted into several overlapping green Gaussian components whose envelope peaks in the 30-31 T region, with P(B_hf) scale dropping from 0.03 in (f) to 0.010 in (h) and (j). The figure demonstrates that Al addition alters local Fe atomic configurations, creating new, lower hyperfine-field components.

observations.observation: The figure is a 5-row x 2-column composite: every left panel is a Mössbauer transmission spectrum and every right panel is the matching P(B_hf) hyperfine-field distribution.
Panel (b) shows a sharp peak near 33 T reaching a P(B_hf) maximum of about 0.08, plus a small hump near 20 T at roughly 0.007.
The caption labels the sample pairs as (a,b) α-Fefoil, (c,d) Fe-5Al, (e,f) Fe-6Al, (g,h) Fe-6.8Al and (i,j) Fe-9Al low-density steels.
The caption states that the humps in P(B_hf) are deconvoluted, and the green component curves are visible as overlapping Gaussians in (d), (f), (h) and (j).
The citing text states that Fe foil gives B_hf peaks at 33 T and ~20 T, the 33 T field corresponding to bcc-Fe with eight Fe first-nearest neighbours and six Fe second-nearest neighbours.
The citing text states that a peak at B_hf = 30.6 T is observed in all studied Fe-Al low-density steel samples.
The citing text states that low-intensity peaks at ~23 T are observed for the Al contents 6, 6.8 and 9, but are absent for Fe-5Al.
The citing text states reference hyperfine fields of 30 T for DO3 (Fe3Al) and 21 T for B2 (FeAl) phases in Fe-Al alloys with Al > 24 wt%.
The vertical scale of the P(B_hf) panels falls progressively along the series: up to 0.08 in (b), 0.02 in (d), 0.03 in (f), and 0.010 in (h) and (j).
In the left column the absorption minima become shallower and the lines broader as Al content increases, from minima near 80.5% in (a) to a nearly flat, shallow sextet in (i).
The right-hand panels' abscissa is labelled B_hf (T) with a range of 18 to 36 T, and the left-hand panels' abscissa is Velocity (mm/s) with ticks from -8 to 8.
No numeric values are printed on the deconvoluted component curves; the individual peak positions and areas are only given in Table 1 according to the citing text.

subfigures.description: Mössbauer spectrum of α-Fe foil: Transmission (%) vs Velocity (mm/s), y from 80 to 100, six sharp absorption lines (bcc Fe sextet) with red data points and black fitted curve; deepest minima reach about 80.5%.
P(B_hf) distribution of α-Fe foil vs B_hf (T), y 0.00-0.08; a weak hump near 20 T and a sharp peak near 33 T at about 0.08.
Mössbauer spectrum of Fe-5Al: Transmission (%) vs Velocity, y 92-100, broader six-line pattern than (a).
P(B_hf) for Fe-5Al, y 0.00-0.02, broad hump deconvoluted into multiple green Gaussian sub-peaks spanning roughly 26-34 T with envelope maxima around 30.5 and 33 T.
Mössbauer spectrum of Fe-6Al: Transmission (%) vs Velocity, y 90-100, six-line pattern with broadened lines.
P(B_hf) for Fe-6Al, y 0.00-0.03, broad asymmetric hump deconvoluted into several green components, envelope peaking near 31 T with a shoulder near 33 T.
Mössbauer spectrum of Fe-6.8Al: Transmission (%) vs Velocity, y 96-100, relatively shallow, broadened sextet.
P(B_hf) for Fe-6.8Al, y 0.000-0.010, broad hump deconvoluted into multiple green Gaussian sub-peaks distributed from about 25 to 34 T.
Mössbauer spectrum of Fe-9Al: Transmission (%) vs Velocity, y 96-100, shallowest and most broadened sextet of the series; carries the shared x-axis label Velocity (mm/s).
P(B_hf) for Fe-9Al, y 0.000-0.010, broad hump deconvoluted into several green components spanning roughly 25-34 T.

unreadable_items: Individual deconvoluted Gaussian component peaks in (d), (f), (h) and (j): positions and intensities are not numerically labelled and can only be read against the gridlines
Exact fitted spectral parameters (isomer shift, quadrupole splitting, line widths) of the Mössbauer spectra are not printed on any panel
